cases.detail: Xezim 0.11.4 evaluates words[1][0][1] of a multidimensional string array containing "BC" as 1 instead of character "C" (67), and returns unknown bits when comparing an out-of-bounds string-array element to the empty string. IEEE 1800-2023 6.16 defines string character indexing and 7.4.5 specifies the empty string for an invalid array index. Array copies and slices satisfy their assertions before the character check fails.

cases.detail: Xezim 0.11.4 evaluates each of the two authored select_word() calls twice and also increments a postfix array index twice while updating string-array elements. The standalone probe prints calls=4 index=2 words=ZXQ,12 instead of calls=2 index=1 words=12,def. IEEE 1800-2023 6.16.2 makes putc equivalent to a character assignment; lowering its read and write must preserve the effects of evaluating the selected destination.
cases.name: string::fixed_array_mutation_indices

cases.detail: Xezim 0.11.4 returns 0 instead of 1 for the checks after copying existing rows into multidimensional string-array assignment patterns. The case exercises row-valued items, an array-valued default, row replication and singleton rows. IEEE 1800-2023 10.9.1 evaluates each item as an assignment to its corresponding element or subarray type. Celox and Verilator pass the case.
